data: Social and Political Thought: Intimations of Modernity

This course deals with ideas articulated by individual thinkers such as Machiavelli, Hobbes, Locke, Mill, Weber and Marx on society, politics, and power. In addition, it covers different ways of thinking of ‘past’, their attendant imaginaries, and the politics of identity and recognition in the modern world.  Both these parts are connected by and anchored in the stories of ‘modernity’. ‘Modernity’ is a large  and complex theme that encompasses transformations in the sphere of economy, politics, society and  morals. It does not offer a unitary story. We also know that it has become a global currency for  justifying as well as critiquing power. Separated by a long stretch of time, how do we make sense of  these ideas? How these thinkers, spanning a period of four centuries, were not only shaped by  significant sociopolitical changes but also created new ways of comprehending them? The course  brings interpretive and methodological resources from sociological theories, political philosophy, and historical imagination to examine ideas and experiences that define ‘modern’ life and their embattled presence in our time
